stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.fps.xne.justification: The project definition exactly matches the blueprint definition: `PowerSeries.XnEquiv n f g` has body `∀ m ≤ n, coeff m f = coeff m g`, corresponding to “each m ∈ {0,1,…,n} satisfies [x^m]f = [x^m]g.” The targets then cover every listed property: `equivalence` gives (a); `add`, `sub`, and `mul` give (b); `smul` gives (c); `invOfUnit` gives (d) over a commutative ring when the constant coefficients are represented by units, while `inv` gives the field specialization under the equivalent nonzero-constant condition; `div` expresses (e) as `a * c.invOfUnit u ≡[x^n] b * d.invOfUnit v`; and `sum` and `prod` give (f). The unit binders and equations, e.g. `(ua ub : Rˣ), constantCoeff a = ↑ua → constantCoeff b = ↑ub`, encode the invertibility assumptions on the power series rather than adding unrelated hypotheses. The `[DecidableEq ι]` binders in `sum` and `prod` are implementation-level encoding for `Finset`. Several declarations are strictly more general than the blueprint’s common coefficient setting—for example, equivalence, addition, multiplication, scalar multiplication, sums, and products only assume `[CommSemiring R]`, while subtraction and unit-based inversion assume `[CommRing R]`; this stronger generality does not impair faithfulness.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.gf.prod.justification: The target quantifies exactly as required: `∀ (n : ℕ)`, matching “Let $n\in\mathbb N$,” and concludes `numDistinctPartitions n = numOddPartitions n`, matching `$d_n=o_n$`. By their bodies, these are `(Nat.Partition.distincts n).card` and `(Nat.Partition.odds n).card`. The base-library definitions say that `Nat.Partition` consists of multisets of positive integers summing to `n`, so order is disregarded; `distincts` requires each part to be used at most once, and `odds` requires every part to be odd while permitting repetitions. Thus the two cardinalities have exactly the meanings assigned to $d_n$ and $o_n$ in the blueprint, with no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.jtp.exc.justification: The two target declarations exactly cover the two conclusions in the blueprint. For every `ell : ℤ`, `{n : ℕ}`, and `mu : n.Partition`, `excitedState_energy` states `(excitedState ell mu).energy = ell.natAbs ^ 2 + 2 * n`; since `Nat.Partition` is a partition whose parts sum to `n`, this `n` is precisely `|λ|`, and `ell.natAbs ^ 2` is the natural-valued form of `ℓ²`. Likewise, `excitedState_parnum` states `(excitedState ell mu).parnum = ell`. The dependency `excitedStateLevels` uses `{p | p < ell - ↑k} ∪ {p | ∃ i, p = ell - 1 - ↑↑i + ...}`, which under the documented integer representation of the half-integer level `p + 1/2` is exactly the informal set of all levels below `ℓ-k` together with the levels `ℓ-i+1/2+λ_i` for one-based `i`. There are no additional hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.jtp.fin.justification: The target states `Function.Bijective fun pair => AlgebraicCombinatorics.State.fromFinsetPair pair.1 pair.2`, exactly matching “The map `(P,N) ↦ fromFinsetPair(P,N)` is a bijection from pairs of finite subsets of ℕ to states.” Here `pair` has domain `Finset ℕ × Finset ℕ`, and `Finset ℕ` represents finite subsets of ℕ. The dependency `fromFinsetPair` defines its levels by `p ≥ 0 ∧ Int.toNat p ∈ P ∨ p < 0 ∧ Int.toNat (-p - 1) ∉ N`, matching the informal encoding of present nonnegative levels and missing negative levels. The codomain `State` has exactly the required finiteness conditions, and the target adds no hypotheses or restrictions.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.jtp.gro.justification: The two target declarations exactly split the blueprint’s conjunction. They quantify without added hypotheses over the required domain: `∀ (ell : ℤ)`. The first concludes `(groundState ell).energy = ell.natAbs ^ 2`, which is the natural-number value of the blueprint’s `energy G_ℓ = ℓ²`; since energy is defined in `ℕ`, `ell.natAbs ^ 2` is precisely the nonnegative square of the integer ℓ. The second concludes `(groundState ell).parnum = ell`, exactly matching `parnum G_ℓ = ℓ`. The dependency `groundState` has levels `{p | p < ell}`; under the stated representation `q = p + 1/2`, this corresponds to the informal set of half-integer levels `q < ℓ`. The formal `energy` and `parnum` bodies likewise use the specified nonnegative-present and negative-missing levels with the correct weights and signed cardinality difference. Thus, taken together, the declarations imply the full informal statement with no contentful restriction or added hypothesis.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.jtp.int.justification: The formal proposition is exactly bijectivity of the advertised global map: `Function.Bijective fun pair => ...excitedState pair.1 pair.2.snd`. Its inferred domain is `ℤ × (Σ n : ℕ, Nat.Partition n)`, which represents an integer together with an arbitrary partition, matching `Φ : ℤ × {partitions} → {states}`. The codomain is `AlgebraicCombinatorics.State`, whose body encodes sets containing only finitely many nonnegative represented levels and omitting only finitely many negative represented levels, exactly matching the informal definition after the documented representation of `p + 1/2` by `p`. Finally, `excitedStateLevels` uses `{p | p < ell - k} ∪ {p | ∃ i, p = ell - 1 - i + parts[i]}` with zero-based `i`; under the half-integer representation this is precisely the informal `E_{ℓ,λ} = {levels < ℓ-k} ∪ {ℓ-i+1/2+λ_i | i=1,…,k}`. Thus the function and its quantified domain and codomain agree with the blueprint, with no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers. The inverse description is the corresponding characterization of the inverse of this bijection, not a conflicting additional restriction.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.jtp.jac.justification: The blueprint says only that the parameterized identity is obtained “by applying the evaluation map `eval_{a,b,u,v}`,” and its definition states no admissibility conditions on these parameters. The elaborated target instead proves the equality only under the contentful hypotheses `a > 0`, `a ≥ |b|`, and `v ≠ 0`. These restrictions enter directly through the target binders `∀ (a b : ℤ), a > 0 → a ≥ |b| → ∀ (u v : ℚ), v ≠ 0 → ...`; they are not merely type-theoretic encoding. In particular, the bodies of `jacobiLHSEval` and `jacobiRHSEval` use `.toNat`, which truncates negative exponents to zero, so the first two assumptions ensure that these bodies represent the displayed nonnegative-exponent FPS formulas, while `v ≠ 0` is needed for evaluating negative Laurent powers of `z`. To be faithful, the informal statement or `def.jtp.evalJacobiCorrect` must explicitly restrict to `a > 0`, `a ≥ |b|`, and `v ≠ 0`. Alternatively, the formal evaluation construction and codomain would need to be generalized to represent arbitrary integer exponents and handle the full parameter range without these hypotheses.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.jtp.jum.justification: Together the two targets exactly formalize the two conclusions in “A jump by q steps keeps the particle number unchanged and raises the energy by 2q”: `jump_parnum` concludes `(S.jump p q hp hpq hq).parnum = S.parnum`, while `jump_energy` concludes `(S.jump p q hp hpq hq).energy = S.energy + 2 * q`. Their binders `hp : p ∈ S.levels`, `hpq : p + ↑q ∉ S.levels`, and `hq : q > 0` are precisely the conditions in the informal jump definition, and `q : ℕ` with `q > 0` encodes a positive integer. The body of `State.jump`, `S.levels \ {p} ∪ {p + ↑q}`, matches the specified set operation. The integer representation of half-integer levels and the bodies of `parnum` and `energy` implement the informal state conventions, including the positive/negative-level boundary. Splitting the informal conjunction into two theorems introduces no drift.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.jtp.par.justification: The blueprint states: “For each ℓ ∈ ℤ, the map Φℓ : {partitions} → {states with particle number ℓ}, λ ↦ Eℓ,λ is a bijection.” The target has exactly the outer quantifier `∀ (ell : ℤ)` and asserts `Function.Bijective fun p => ⟨AlgebraicCombinatorics.State.excitedState ell p.snd, ⋯⟩`. Here the dependent pair of an index and `n.Partition` represents an arbitrary partition, while the constructed subtype element represents a state satisfying `S.parnum = ell`; this is justified by `excitedState_parnum`. The formal `excitedStateLevels` body also agrees with the informal half-integer convention: its integer representatives `{p | p < ell - k}` and `ell - 1 - i + μᵢ` correspond respectively to levels below `ℓ-k` and to `ℓ-(i+1)+1/2+μᵢ`. The definitions of `State` and `parnum` likewise translate positive half-integer levels to representatives `p ≥ 0` and negative ones to `p < 0`. There are no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.lgv.kpa.justification: The elaborated binders exactly cover the blueprint data: `∀ {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing K] {k : ℕ} (w : LGV.ArcWeight LGV.integerLattice K) (A B : LGV.kVertex (ℤ × ℤ) k)`, matching “Let K be a commutative ring,” an arbitrary weight for each lattice arc, `k ∈ ℕ`, and two k-vertices `A` and `B`. The dependency `integerLattice` has precisely the east and north arcs specified by the informal lattice definition. On the left, `pathWeightMatrix ... w A B` has entry `pathWeightSum ... w (A i) (B j)`, and `pathWeightSum` sums `pathWeight` over all paths between those vertices; `pathWeight` is the product of arc weights. Thus its determinant is exactly the displayed determinant in the blueprint. On the right, `∑ σ, Equiv.Perm.sign σ • nipatWeightSum ... w A (permuteKVertex σ B) σ` ranges over every permutation of `Fin k`; `sign σ` is ±1 according to parity, `permuteKVertex σ B i = B (σ i)`, and `nipatWeightSum` sums `pathTupleWeight` over `nipatFinset`, whose underlying predicate requires that no two component paths share a vertex. This matches `∑_{σ ∈ S_k} (-1)^σ` times the sum of tuple weights over nipats from `A` to `σ(B)`. The supplied path-finiteness theorem and decidable-equality instances merely encode the finite sums and impose no additional mathematical hypothesis.

The formal binders match the blueprint: `∀ {K} [CommRing K] ... {D : LGV.SimpleDigraph V} (hpf : D.IsPathFinite), D.IsAcyclic → ∀ {k} (w : LGV.ArcWeight D K) (A B : LGV.kVertex V k)` corresponds to “Let K be a commutative ring,” “D be a path-finite ... acyclic digraph,” arc weights, arbitrary `k ∈ ℕ`, and two k-tuples. The conclusion also matches definitionally: `pathWeightMatrix` has entries `pathWeightSum ... (A i) (B j)`, which sums the products of arc weights over paths; `nipatWeightSum ... A (permuteKVertex σ B) σ` sums `pathTupleWeight` over tuples whose component paths share no vertex; and `permuteKVertex σ B i = B (σ i)` is exactly the stated `σ(B)`. Finally, `Equiv.Perm.sign σ • ...` realizes the factor `(-1)^σ`, and the outer finite sum ranges over all permutations of `Fin k`, the zero-based encoding of `S_k`. The additional `[DecidableEq V]` is computational/encoding infrastructure needed for path-intersection predicates and finite-set sums, not a mathematically substantive restriction. Although the formal graph type is `SimpleDigraph`, its only explicit simplicity condition excludes loops, and acyclicity already excludes any loop arc under the supplied path and acyclicity definitions, so this does not narrow the acyclic case asserted by the blueprint.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.eu.justification: The binder `∀ n > 0` matches “for each positive integer n.” The subtype index `{ k // pentagonalNumber k < n }` represents exactly the integers satisfying `w_k < n`, and `(ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1)` is the sum of first powers of divisors, hence the stated sum-of-divisors function. The formal signs `(-1) ^ (↑k).natAbs` and, in the exceptional case, `(-1) ^ (k.natAbs + 1)` agree with `(-1)^k` and `(-1)^(k-1)` respectively by parity; in the exceptional case positivity of `n = w_k` excludes `k = 0`. The body of `pentagonalNumber` implements `((3*k - 1)*k)/2`, and `pentagonalNumberInverse` searches sufficient finite ranges to return an index exactly when positive `n` equals some `w_k`. Thus its `some k` and `none` branches faithfully encode the two cases in the blueprint.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.jt.justification: The target has no added binders or hypotheses and asserts exactly `AlgebraicCombinatorics.jacobiLHS' = AlgebraicCombinatorics.jacobiRHS'`. Its ambient type is `JacobiRing`, whose body is `PowerSeries (LaurentPolynomial ℤ)`, matching “in the ring `(ℤ[z^{±}])[[q]]`.” The left side unfolds to `∏' (n : ℕ), jacobiProductTerm n`, with factors `1 + X^(2*n+1) * jacobiZ`, `1 + X^(2*n+1) * jacobiZInv`, and `1 - X^(2*(n+1))`; indexing `n : ℕ` from zero is exactly the reindexing of the blueprint’s `n>0` factors with exponents `2n-1, 2n-1, 2n`. Here `jacobiZ = C (T 1)` and `jacobiZInv = C (T (-1))`, so these are `z` and `z⁻¹`. The right side unfolds to `∑' (ell : ℤ), X ^ ell.natAbs ^ 2 * C (T ell)`, which is `∑_{ℓ∈ℤ} q^{ℓ²}z^ℓ`. Thus the formal definitions reproduce both sides of the stated identity without a mathematically contentful restriction or extra assumption.

The binders match the blueprint exactly: formal `∀ (a b : ℤ), a > 0 → a ≥ |b| → ∀ (u v : ℚ), v ≠ 0 → ...` corresponds to “Let a and b be two integers such that a>0 and a≥|b|. Let u,v∈ℚ ... with v≠0.” The dependency bodies correctly expand the stated substitution `q = ux^a`, `z = vx^b`: `jacobiLHSEval` indexes `n>0` by `n := k+1` and uses coefficients and exponents `u^(2n-1)v·x^((2n-1)a+b)`, `u^(2n-1)v⁻¹·x^((2n-1)a-b)`, and `u^(2n)·x^(2na)`; `jacobiRHSEval` uses `(u ^ (ℓ ^ 2).natAbs * v ^ ℓ) • X ^ (a * ℓ ^ 2 + b * ℓ).toNat`. Under `a > 0` and `a ≥ |b|`, all these integer exponents are nonnegative, so the uses of `.toNat` do not truncate negative exponents; `(ℓ^2).natAbs` likewise represents the nonnegative exponent ℓ². Thus the target equality `jacobiLHSEval ... = jacobiRHSEval ...` is precisely the displayed product–sum identity in `PowerSeries ℚ`, with no added mathematical hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.ma.justification: The blueprint specifically asserts an identity “In the FPS ring ℤ[[x]]”, whereas the elaborated target quantifies `∀ {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] ... [IsTopologicalSemiring R]`. This is not a harmless generalization containing the stated case: ℤ is a commutative ring, not a `CommSemiring`, and the supplied `IsTopologicalSemiring` documentation explicitly directs rings to `IsTopologicalRing`. Thus the declaration cannot be specialized to the blueprint’s coefficient ring. The `HasProd ... (PowerSeries.mk fun n => ↑(partitionCount n))` conclusion otherwise appropriately gives the product’s convergence to the partition generating series, and the `k + 1` indexing matches `k = 1,2,…`. To make it faithful, change the target’s coefficient structure to one admitting ℤ—most directly state it for `PowerSeries ℤ` with an appropriate Hausdorff topological-ring structure, or use commutative-ring/`IsTopologicalRing` binders that include ℤ.

The coefficient of the left-hand side is exactly the blueprint sum: `∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), ↑(Nat.Partition.partsCount k n)` ranges over `k = 0, …, m`, and `partsCount` is defined by `fun k n => {p | p.parts.card = k}.card`, matching `p_k(n)`. The right-hand side `∏ k ∈ Finset.range m, ∑' (j : ℕ), PowerSeries.X ^ ((k + 1) * j)` ranges over `k+1 = 1, …, m` and represents each geometric factor `1/(1-x^(k+1))` by `∑_{j≥0} x^((k+1)j)`. Thus it matches `∏_{k=1}^m 1/(1-x^k)`, including the empty-product case `m = 0`. The binders `{R} [CommSemiring R] [TopologicalSpace R] [T2Space R] [IsTopologicalSemiring R]` provide a polymorphic coefficient semiring and the topology needed to express `∑'`; they are encoding conditions for this representation of the infinite geometric series, not extra combinatorial hypotheses on `m`. Quantifying over every such `R` is more general than the blueprint’s unqualified formal-series identity.

The informal statement assumes “I be a subset of {1,2,3,…}” and counts partitions whose parts belong to I. The formal dependency defines `partsInCount I n` as `(Nat.Partition.restricted n fun x => x ∈ I).card`, and `Nat.Partition.restricted` selects exactly those partitions for which every part satisfies membership in `I`, so the coefficients agree with `p_I(n)`. The target’s factor at index `k` is conditional on `k + 1 ∈ I` and is `∑' j, X ^ ((k + 1) * j)`, exactly the geometric-series factor for the positive part `k+1`; indices not in I contribute `1`. Thus `HasProd ... (PowerSeries.mk fun n => ↑(partsInCount I n))` expresses the stated product as the generating series. Although the formal binder is `(I : Set ℕ)` rather than restricting I to positive naturals, this is a harmless generalization: the shifted product only tests positive numbers `k+1`, and partition parts are positive, so membership of `0` affects neither side. The binders `[DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ I]` and `[TopologicalSpace R] [T2Space R] [IsTopologicalSemiring R]` supply decidability and the convergence setting needed for `ite`, `tsum`, and `HasProd`; they encode the formal realization of the infinite formal-power-series product rather than changing the combinatorial identity. Quantification over every suitable commutative semiring `R` is also a generalization of the coefficient identity.

The finite-product target quantifies exactly over “(m : ℕ)” and states `∏ k ∈ Finset.range m, ∑' (j : ℕ), PowerSeries.X ^ ((k + 1) * j)`, which indexes k+1 through 1,…,m and gives the geometric factors ∑_{j≥0} x^{(k+1)j} = 1/(1-x^{k+1}). Its coefficient series is `PowerSeries.mk fun n => ↑(Nat.Partition.restricted n fun x => x ≤ m).card`, exactly the number of partitions of n all of whose parts are ≤ m. The `HasProd` version is equivalent in indexing: `if k + 1 ≤ m then ... else 1` makes only k=0,…,m−1 nontrivial, and `partsLeqCount m n` unfolds to the same restricted-partition cardinality. Quantification over an arbitrary coefficient `CommSemiring R` is a generalization via casting the natural counts. The topology, `T2Space`, and `IsTopologicalSemiring` binders support the chosen `tsum`/`HasProd` encoding of the infinite geometric sums and product; they encode that presentation rather than impose a combinatorial restriction on m or the partitions.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.od.justification: The target `oddPartsCount_eq_distinctPartsCount` states `∀ (n : ℕ), Nat.Partition.oddPartsCount n = Nat.Partition.distinctPartsCount n`, exactly matching “for each `n ∈ ℕ`, `p_odd(n) = p_dist(n)`.” Its dependencies unfold to `(Nat.Partition.odds n).card` and `(Nat.Partition.distincts n).card`; the supplied library definitions identify these as the finite sets of partitions whose parts are respectively all odd and each used at most once, matching the informal definitions of odd and distinct parts. Equivalently, the second target states this unfolded equality directly: `∀ (n : ℕ), (Nat.Partition.odds n).card = (Nat.Partition.distincts n).card`. There are no added hypotheses or restricted quantifiers.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.pe.justification: The target states exactly `AlgebraicCombinatorics.eulerProduct = AlgebraicCombinatorics.pentagonalSeries`, matching the blueprint equality `∏_{k=1}^∞ (1-x^k) = ∑_{k∈ℤ} (-1)^k x^{w_k}`. The dependency `eulerProduct` is `∏' (k : ℕ), (1 - PowerSeries.X ^ (k + 1))`, so its shifted natural-number index is precisely the product over positive integers. The dependency `pentagonalSeries` assigns coefficient `(-1) ^ k.natAbs` when `n` is the generalized pentagonal number `pentagonalNumber k = ((3*k-1)*k/2).toNat`, and zero otherwise, which coefficientwise represents the stated sum over `k ∈ ℤ`; using `natAbs` preserves the sign for negative integer indices. The use of formal power series and the discrete/pointwise topology is an encoding of the infinite formal product, not an additional mathematical hypothesis. The elaborated target has no added binders or restrictions.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.qb.justification: The blueprint asks for the identity for every commutative ring K, a,b ∈ K, and n ∈ ℕ, as an equality in K[q]. The Lean signature quantifies more generally over “∀ {K : Type u_1} [CommRing K] (a b q : K) (n : ℕ)” and proves the corresponding evaluated identity in K for every element q. Instantiating the formal carrier K with the polynomial ring from the blueprint, taking a and b to be constant polynomials and q to be its indeterminate, yields exactly the stated polynomial identity. Thus the elementwise theorem is stronger, not weaker. The finite ranges also agree: “Finset.range n” gives exponents 0,…,n−1 on the left, while “Finset.range (n + 1)” gives k=0,…,n on the right. On that latter range, the natural-number expressions k−1 and n−k have the intended values. Finally, the dependency `qBinomial q n k` uses the q-Pascal recurrence with base cases 1 and 0, matching the blueprint’s Gaussian coefficient on 0 ≤ k ≤ n.

The formal binders exactly encode the blueprint setting: `∀ {L} [CommRing L] {A} [Ring A] [Algebra L A] (ω : L) (a b : A)` corresponds to “Let L be a commutative ring… Let A be a noncommutative L-algebra. Let a,b∈A.” Here `Ring A` is the supplied noncommutative-ring notion (commutativity is not required), while `Algebra L A` provides the stated scalar action and compatibility. The hypothesis `b * a = ω • (a * b)` is precisely “ba = ω ab”. The conclusion quantifies `∀ (n : ℕ)` and sums over `Finset.range (n + 1)`, i.e. exactly `k = 0,…,n`, with summand `qBinomial ω n k • (a ^ k * b ^ (n - k))`. The dependency’s recurrence `[n choose k]_q = [n-1 choose k-1]_q + q^k [n-1 choose k]_q`, together with its boundary values, agrees with the blueprint’s partition-defined Gaussian coefficient on this range. Allowing `A` also to happen to be commutative is not a restriction and is consistent with “noncommutative ring” meaning multiplication is not assumed commutative.

Part (a), `qBinomial_quot_formula`, is faithful and more general than the blueprint: its binders `∀ {R} [CommRing R] (n k : ℕ), k ≤ n → ∀ (q : R)` assert exactly the cross-multiplied product identity over any commutative ring, with `Finset.range k` producing the exponents `1,…,k` and `n,…,n-k+1`. However, part (b), `qBinomial_eq_prod_quot`, narrows the ambient algebra through the binder `[inst : Field R]`. The blueprint explicitly allows the quotient identity “in the ring ℤ[[q]] or in the field of rational functions over ℚ,” and its fraction definition only requires the relevant denominators to be invertible; it does not require the entire ambient ring to be a field. The hypothesis `(∀ i ∈ Finset.range k, q^(i+1) ≠ 1)` correctly guarantees nonzero denominators in a field, but `[Field R]` is stronger than the needed invertibility assumptions and excludes the stated formal-power-series ring. Thus the difference enters in the `Field R` binder of `qBinomial_eq_prod_quot`. To make it faithful to both stated settings, formulate part (b) over `[CommRing R]` with hypotheses that each `1 - q^(i+1)` is a unit, expressing division via those units, or provide explicit specializations to `ℤ[[q]]` and to the rational-function field.

The blueprint assumes “Let n,k∈ℕ with n≥k,” matching the formal binders `(n k : ℕ), k ≤ n`. Its second displayed equality is exactly the target conclusion `qBinomial n k q = qFactorial n q / (qFactorial k q * qFactorial (n - k) q)`, with `qInt` and `qFactorial` having the stated blueprint definitions. Although the target uses an arbitrary `[Field R]` and assumes `(∀ i ∈ Finset.range n, q ^ (i + 1) ≠ 1)`, this is a generalization to evaluations at field elements for which the displayed quotients are valid; for the blueprint’s indeterminate in the rational-function field, these nonvanishing conditions are automatic. The omitted intermediate quotient follows algebraically by splitting `[n]_q!` into `[n-k]_q!` times `[n-k+1]_q⋯[n]_q` and cancelling the nonzero factors ensured by the hypothesis. Thus the formal theorem implies the stated chain in the rational-function interpretation allowed by “in … rational functions over ℚ”.

Both declarations add the mathematically substantive binder `∀ (k : ℕ), 0 < k →`, whereas the blueprint says “Let `k ∈ ℕ`” with no positivity restriction. Thus they omit `k = 0`. In the blueprint, `qBinomial` has an integer lower index, so at `k = 0` the term `\binom{n-1}{k-1}_q = \binom{n-1}{-1}_q` is zero by the negative-index convention, and both recurrences remain valid. The project declaration `AlgebraicCombinatorics.qBinomial : ℕ → ℕ → R → R` instead restricts the lower index to `ℕ`; Lean’s saturating `k - 1` becomes `0` at `k = 0`, so it cannot directly represent that negative-index term. Consequently, merely removing `0 < k` from either target would produce the wrong boundary formula. To make the formalization faithful, introduce an integer-indexed extension of `qBinomial` that returns zero for negative lower indices and quantify `k : ℕ` without `0 < k`, or state an equivalent boundary-aware formula using `if k = 0 then 0 else qBinomial (n - 1) (k - 1) q`. The use of arbitrary `[CommSemiring R]` and `q : R` is a valid strengthening/generalization of the commutative-ring specialization and is not the source of drift.

The binders `[Field F] [Fintype F]` exactly express “Let F be a finite field,” while `[AddCommGroup V] [Module F V] [Module.Finite F V]` together with `Module.finrank F V = n` express that V is an n-dimensional F-vector space. The conclusion `qBinomial (↑(Fintype.card F)) n k = ↑(Nat.card { W // Module.finrank F ↥W = k })` evaluates the Gaussian coefficient at |F| and equates it with the cardinality of the subtype of submodules W having dimension k. Although the equality is represented after casting both natural-valued quantities into ℚ, this preserves the intended numerical equality. Using `Nat.card` is also appropriate here: over a finite field, a finite-dimensional vector space has only finitely many subspaces. Finally, the recurrence in the body of `qBinomial` is the Gaussian-binomial recurrence corresponding to the blueprint’s partition-polynomial definition, including the expected zero values when k > n.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.si.justification: The formal binder `∀ (n : ℕ)` matches “For any `n ∈ ℕ`.” Its left side is exactly `n * partitionCount n`, where `partitionCount n = Fintype.card n.Partition`, matching `n p(n)`. On the right, `k ∈ Finset.range n` means `0 ≤ k < n`; setting `j = k + 1` makes `j` range from `1` through `n`. Thus `divisorSum (k + 1) * partitionCount (n - k - 1)` is `σ(j) p(n-j)`. Here `divisorSum = ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1`, whose documented meaning is the sum of first powers of positive divisors. Natural-number subtraction causes no discrepancy because `k < n` throughout the sum. The case `n = 0` also agrees: both sides are zero and the sum is empty.

The binder `∀ (I : Set ℕ) ... (∀ i ∈ I, i > 0)` exactly represents “Let I be a subset of {1,2,3,…}”; `[DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ I]` is only computational encoding needed by `Nat.Partition.restricted` and `Finset.filter`, not a mathematical restriction. By the library definitions, `(Nat.Partition.restricted n fun x => x ∈ I).card` is precisely the number `p_I(n)` of partitions of `n` all of whose parts lie in `I`. On the right, `k ∈ Finset.range n` means `k = 0,…,n−1`; after reindexing by `m = k+1`, `(∑ d ∈ (k + 1).divisors with d ∈ I, d)` is `σ_I(m)` and `restricted (n-k-1)` is `p_I(n-m)`. Thus the displayed formal sum is exactly `∑_{m=1}^n σ_I(m) p_I(n-m)`. The formal quantifier `∀ (n : ℕ)` also matches “For any n ∈ ℕ,” including `n = 0`, where both sides are zero.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pars.x-.justification: The target states exactly `PowerSeries.X * (PowerSeries.derivative ℤ) Nat.Partition.P = Nat.Partition.S * Nat.Partition.P`, matching the blueprint’s “the generating function identity $X\cdot P' = S\cdot P$ … as an equality of formal power series in $\mathbb Z[[x]]$.” The referenced series also agree with the informal definitions: `P : PowerSeries ℤ` has body `Nat.Partition.genFun fun x x_1 => 1`, whose constant character counts each partition with weight 1, and `S : PowerSeries ℤ` has coefficient 0 at index 0 and `↑(Nat.Partition.divisorSum n)` otherwise. Finally, `divisorSum n = (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n`, matching $\sigma(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}d$. There are no additional binders or hypotheses restricting the statement.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.perm.ca.justification: The informal statement requires both that the canonical word has length ℓ(σ) and that “its product is σ.” The formal conclusion is only `Equiv.Perm.IsReduced σ.canonicalReducedWord`, which unfolds via `IsReduced` to `List.length σ.canonicalReducedWord = (Equiv.Perm.wordProd σ.canonicalReducedWord).length`. This compares the word’s length with the inversion length of its own product; it does not state `Equiv.Perm.wordProd σ.canonicalReducedWord = σ`, and consequently does not directly state that its length is `σ.length`. The difference is in the TARGET conclusion, not in an added binder. To match the blueprint, the conclusion should additionally assert `Equiv.Perm.wordProd σ.canonicalReducedWord = σ` and, either directly or through `IsReduced`, that `List.length σ.canonicalReducedWord = σ.length`; for example, a conjunction of the product equality with `IsReduced σ.canonicalReducedWord` would express the intended content.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.perm.dc.justification: The package weakens and restricts the blueprint in several places. For (b), the blueprint asserts that “Any two DCDs of σ can be obtained from each other” by swapping cycles and rotating them, whereas `dcd_unique_cycleType` concludes only `Multiset.map (fun c => c.support.card) cycs.val = σ.cycleType`. Equality of the multiset of cycle lengths does not express, and is strictly weaker than, equivalence of the actual cycles under swapping and rotation. This declaration should instead quantify over two list-based DCDs and assert equality modulo an outer permutation and rotations of the inner lists. For (c), `canonicalDcd_exists_unique` adds the binder `[Inhabited α]`, while the blueprint covers “any totally ordered finite set,” including the empty set. This is a mathematically contentful restriction introduced solely because the predicate uses `List.head!`; the empty ordered finite type has the unique empty DCD. Faithfulness would require removing `[Inhabited α]` and replacing `head!` with a head/minimum construction justified by the existing hypotheses `l ≠ []`. Moreover, for (a), `exists_dcd` witnesses a `Finset (Equiv.Perm α)` of nonidentity `IsCycle`s and gives disjointness and a product equation, but does not directly witness the blueprint’s `List (List α)` with nonempty entries and the explicit condition that every element of `X` occurs exactly once; in particular fixed points are omitted from `IsCycle` factors because `IsCycle` is nonidentity, while the blueprint represents them by singleton lists. A direct faithful declaration would use list representatives with nonemptiness, `flatten.Nodup`, universal membership in the flattening, and the `dcdListToPerm` product equation, as in the predicate used by the third target.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.perm.le.justification: The decisive target is `lehmerCode_bijective`: `∀ (n : ℕ), Function.Bijective fun σ => ⟨AlgebraicCombinatorics.Perm.lehmerCode σ, ⋯⟩`, which states exactly that the map from `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` (the permutations of an n-element set, hence `S_n`) to the subtype determined by `lehmerCodeSet n` is bijective. The dependency defines that codomain by `∀ (i : Fin n), f i ≤ n - 1 - ↑i`; under the standard zero-based representation `Fin n = {0,…,n-1}`, index `i` represents the informal position `i+1`, so this bound is the informal `j_{i+1} ≤ n-(i+1)`. Likewise, `lehmerCode` uses `lehmerEntry σ i = {j | i < j ∧ σ i > σ j}.card`, matching the blueprint definition of each Lehmer entry. The additional target `lehmerCode_injective` proves only the injective component and would not alone imply the blueprint’s bijection claim, but it does not weaken or alter the accompanying `lehmerCode_bijective` declaration, which directly formalizes the stated theorem.

The blueprint says “ℓ(σ) is exactly the minimum word length for σ,” which requires both a word representing σ of length ℓ(σ) and a lower bound for every word representing σ. The target only states `∀ {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)), σ.length = List.length ⋯.choose`: equality with the length of one witness selected by `Exists.choose`. That witness comes from `Equiv.Perm.exists_reduced_word`, while `Equiv.Perm.IsReduced` is defined as `List.length w = (Equiv.Perm.wordProd w).length`; thus the declaration identifies ℓ(σ) with one chosen representing word’s length, but does not assert that every `w` satisfying `Equiv.Perm.wordProd w = σ` has `σ.length ≤ List.length w`. To be faithful, the target should additionally quantify over all representing words and state this lower bound, together with existence of a representing word attaining equality, or equate `σ.length` with a formally defined minimum over their lengths.

Part (a) is expressed by `∀ {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)), ∃ w, Equiv.Perm.IsReduced w ∧ Equiv.Perm.wordProd w = σ`. Expanding `IsReduced`, the witness satisfies `List.length w = (wordProd w).length`; using `wordProd w = σ`, it is a product of exactly `σ.length` simple transpositions. Here `length σ = σ.inversions.card`, matching the blueprint’s ℓ(σ), and `Word n = List (Fin (n - 1))` indexes exactly the adjacent transpositions (with the harmless zero-based relabeling of `[n]` as `Fin n`). Part (b), `∀ {n : ℕ} (w : Equiv.Perm.Word n), (Equiv.Perm.wordProd w).length ≤ List.length w`, is a more general formulation of the required lower bound: whenever a word `w` of length `p` represents a fixed `σ`, it yields `ℓ(σ) ≤ p`. Combined with part (a), which supplies a representation with `p = ℓ(σ)`, this says precisely that ℓ(σ) is the smallest possible number of simples. The empty list has product `1`, so the stated zero-simple identity case is also represented.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pie.1.justification: The blueprint quantifies over a finite universe `U` and finitely many subsets `A_i`, while the Lean signature quantifies over a finite type `[Fintype α]`, a finite index set `(s : Finset ι)`, and a family `(A : ι → Finset α)`. Taking `α` as the finite universe `U` and `s` as `[n]` gives the blueprint case; allowing an arbitrary finite index set `s` is a harmless strict generalization. The formal left side `↑(s.inf fun i => (A i)ᶜ).card` counts elements lying in every complement, hence in none of the indexed sets. The right side `∑ I ∈ s.powerset, (-1) ^ I.card * ↑(I.inf A).card` ranges over all `I ⊆ s` and gives the required alternating cardinality sum. By the supplied signature of `Finset.inf`, its empty infimum uses `OrderTop`; for `Finset α` this is the whole finite universe, matching the blueprint clause `⋂_{i ∈ ∅} A_i = U`. The binders `[DecidableEq α] [Fintype α]` encode finite-set operations and complement on the finite universe rather than adding a mathematically substantive hypothesis.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pie.2.justification: The formal binders `[Fintype ι] ... [Fintype U] ... [AddCommGroup G] (A : ι → Finset U) (w : U → G)` faithfully represent a finite family of subsets of a finite universe, an additive abelian group, and a weight map. The left side `∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.inf fun i => (A i)ᶜ, w u` sums over the intersection of all complements, matching “u ∉ A_i for all i ∈ [n]”. The right side ranges over `Finset.univ.powerset`, i.e. all subsets `I` of the index set, and uses `(-1) ^ I.card • ∑ u ∈ I.inf A, w u`, matching the alternating coefficient and intersection condition. Quantifying over an arbitrary finite index type `ι` is strictly more general than indexing by `[n]`, so it is faithful. The `DecidableEq` binders are computational encoding needed for `Finset` operations, not mathematically substantive restrictions.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pie.2.e.justification: The formal equality exactly expresses the weighted inclusion–exclusion formula. The left side, `∑ u ∈ s.inf fun i => (A i)ᶜ, w u`, sums over the finite universe `U` those `u` lying in every complement `(A i)ᶜ` for `i ∈ s`, matching “`u ∉ A_i ∀ i ∈ s`.” The right side, `∑ I ∈ s.powerset, (-1) ^ I.card • ∑ u ∈ I.inf A, w u`, ranges over all `I ⊆ s`, uses the sign `(-1)^{|I|}`, and sums over the intersection of the `A_i` for `i ∈ I`. For empty `s` or `I`, `Finset.inf` uses the top element of `Finset U`, namely the whole finite universe, as required by vacuous universal quantification. The binders `[Fintype U] [DecidableEq U]` encode that `U` is finite and permit finite-set complements; `[AddCommGroup G]` is exactly the additive abelian-group assumption. `[DecidableEq ι]` is representation infrastructure for `s : Finset ι`. Although `A : ι → Finset U` is defined on a larger ambient type rather than only on `s`, the formula accesses it only at indices in `s`, so this is a harmless encoding and, as the docstring notes, allows a more general ambient index type.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pie.cou.justification: The blueprint asserts both equalities: “D_n = ∑_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k binom(n,k) (n-k)! = n! · ∑_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k/k!.” The target concludes only `↑(numDerangements n) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ k * ↑(n.choose k) * ↑(n - k).factorial`, which faithfully captures the first equality (`range (n + 1)` gives `0 ≤ k ≤ n`) but omits the second factorial-reciprocal formula. Thus the target has a weaker conclusion. The difference enters in the body of `numDerangements_formula`, not through any binder. To make it faithful, the theorem should additionally assert—naturally after casting to a field such as ℚ—that this value equals `n! * ∑_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k / k!`.

The target quantifies exactly as required, `∀ (n : ℕ)`, and states an equality in `ℚ` because both `numDerangements n` and `n.factorial` are cast using `Nat.cast` with target `Rat`. Its sum is over `k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1)`; since `Finset.range m` contains precisely the naturals less than `m`, this is exactly `k = 0, …, n`. The summand `(-1) ^ k / ↑k.factorial` is rational exponentiation and division, hence exactly `(-1)^k/k!`. Finally, `numDerangements n` is documented as the number of derangements of an `n`-element set, matching `D_n`. There are no added hypotheses or restricted quantifiers.

The binders `∀ (m n : ℕ)` exactly match “Let n, m ∈ ℕ.” The dependency `numSurj m n := Fintype.card { f // Function.Surjective f }` counts surjective functions `Fin m → Fin n`; these are equinumerous with maps `[m] → [n]`, since `Fin r` and the blueprint’s `[r] = {1,…,r}` are both canonical `r`-element sets, including at `r = 0`. On the right, `Finset.range (n + 1)` is precisely the inclusive range `k = 0,…,n`; `Nat.choose n k` agrees with the stated binomial coefficient for natural `n,k`; and the casts place the identity in `ℤ`, so `(-1)^k` and `↑n - ↑k` have the intended integer meanings. Because every indexed `k` satisfies `k ≤ n`, this difference represents the blueprint’s nonnegative `n-k`. Thus the formal equality expresses exactly the stated surjection-count formula.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pie.eul.justification: The binder `∀ (c : ℕ), 0 < c →` matches “Let c be a positive integer.” By the docstring for `Nat.totient`, `↑c.totient` is the cardinality of the naturals below `c` coprime to `c`; for positive `c` this has the same cardinality as the coprime elements of `[c] = {1,…,c}`. The conclusion `↑c.totient = ↑c * ∏ p ∈ c.primeFactors, (1 - 1 / ↑p)` is precisely the blueprint’s first equality, with the distinct primes represented canonically by `c.primeFactors` and arithmetic performed in `ℚ`. Although the displayed conclusion does not explicitly include `= ∏ᵢ (pᵢ^{aᵢ} - pᵢ^{aᵢ-1})`, that equality follows from the assumed prime factorization `c = ∏ᵢ pᵢ^{aᵢ}` and `pᵃ(1 - 1/p) = pᵃ - p^{a-1}` for positive `a`. Thus the formal theorem implies the entire blueprint chain and introduces no additional hypothesis.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pie.moe.justification: The formal hypothesis exactly matches the blueprint: `(∀ I ⊆ S, b I = ∑ J ∈ I.powerset, a J)` states `b_I = ∑_{J ⊆ I} a_J` for every `I ⊆ S`, since `I.powerset` is the finset of all subsets of `I`. Its conclusion `(∀ I ⊆ S, a I = ∑ J ∈ I.powerset, (-1) ^ (I \ J).card • b J)` likewise states `a_I = ∑_{J ⊆ I} (-1)^{|I \ J|} b_J`. The binder `[AddCommGroup A]` is precisely the informal “additive abelian group.” `[DecidableEq α]` is an encoding requirement for finset difference, not an additional mathematical restriction on the finite set. Although `a b : Finset α → A` are defined on all finite subsets of `α`, the hypothesis and conclusion only inspect indices contained in `S`; this harmlessly extends the subset-indexed families from the blueprint and does not weaken the asserted inversion formula.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.pol.eva.justification: All seven targets restrict the algebra to `[inst_1 : CommRing A]`, whereas the blueprint says “Let A be a K-algebra” and its definition explicitly makes A a “(noncommutative) ring.” Thus the formal declarations cover only commutative K-algebras and do not imply the claims for arbitrary blueprint K-algebras. The restriction enters already through `FPS.polyEval`, whose type requires `{A} → [CommRing A] → [Algebra K A]`, even though its body is `Polynomial.aeval a f` and `Polynomial.aeval` only requires a `Semiring A`. Generalize `FPS.polyEval` and the targets from `[CommRing A]` to a typeclass supporting arbitrary rings (or even `[Semiring A]`, which would be a faithful stronger generalization), while retaining `[Algebra K A]`. Apart from this narrowed typeclass binder, the seven displayed identities match parts (a)–(f), including `Polynomial.C c` evaluating to `algebraMap K A c`, i.e. the scalar `c · 1_A`.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.qbinom_.justification: The target quantifies exactly as the blueprint does: `∀ (n k : ℕ)`, matching “Let `n, k ∈ ℕ`.” Its conclusion is precisely the stated case distinction: `if Even n ∧ Odd k then 0 else (n / 2).choose (k / 2)`, where natural-number division by `2` gives the two floors and `Nat.choose` is the ordinary binomial coefficient. `Polynomial.eval (-1) ...` realizes the blueprint notation `\binom n k_{-1}` over `ℤ`. The project definition of `qBinomial` is the standard subset-sum form of the same Gaussian polynomial: a `k`-subset of `{0,…,n-1}` corresponds to a partition fitting in the `k × (n-k)` rectangle, with exponent `S.sum id - (Finset.range k).sum id` equal to the partition size. There are no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.qbinomi.justification: The blueprint quantifies over a general ring: “for all n, k ∈ ℕ and ring element q,” and its defining clause says, “If a is any element of a ring A.” The elaborated target instead has the binder `∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] ...`, restricting the claim to commutative rings. This is a mathematically contentful added hypothesis, not merely statement-level encoding, since the partition sum and recurrence can be formulated for an element of a noncommutative ring as well. The restriction enters through the `[CommRing R]` binders of both `qBinomialEval` and `qBinomial`, and consequently the target. To make the formalization faithful, generalize those dependency binders and the theorem binder to `Ring R` (or another structure covering every blueprint ring while supporting the required finite sums, powers, and integer casts). The natural-number quantifiers `(n k : ℕ)` otherwise match the theorem statement.

The target quantifies exactly over the intended parameter, `∀ (k : ℕ)`. Its product `∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (1 - PowerSeries.X ^ (i + 1))⁻¹` indexes `i = 0,…,k-1`, hence has exponents `1,…,k`, matching `∏_{i=1}^{k} 1/(1-q^i)`. The right side `PowerSeries.mk fun n => ↑(partitionCountAtMostKParts n k)` is the formal power series whose nth coefficient is the partition count, matching `∑_{n=0}^∞ |{p ⊢ n : at most k parts}| · q^n`. In particular, the dependency defines that coefficient as `Nat.card { p // p.parts.card ≤ k }`; `Nat.Partition` denotes partitions of `n`, and `p.parts.card ≤ k` is exactly “at most k parts.” The use of formal power series over `ℚ` is an encoding of the coefficient counts and introduces no additional mathematical hypothesis or narrowed combinatorial quantifier.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.recurre.justification: The target quantifies exactly as required, `∀ (n : ℕ)`, and concludes `exampleRecurrence n = 2 ^ (n + 1) - (n + 1)`, matching “For all n∈ℕ, a_n = 2^{n+1} - (n+1).” The dependency `exampleRecurrence` implements the stated sequence: at `0` it returns `1`, and at `n.succ` it returns `2 * x.1 + n`, where the recursive predecessor value `x.1` is a_n, matching `a_{n+1} = 2a_n + n`. Although formal subtraction is natural-number subtraction and hence truncated, this causes no semantic difference here because `2^(n+1) ≥ n+1` for every natural n.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.all-.justification: The target exactly formalizes the stated implication: its binders require `AlgebraicCombinatorics.IsSemistandard T → SymmetricFunctions.allEntriesZero T → ∀ (n : ℕ), AlgebraicCombinatorics.IsYamanouchi (SymmetricFunctions.rowPartitionFun N n hN) T`, matching “If T is a semistandard tableau with all entries equal to 0, then T is ν-Yamanouchi for the row partition ν = (n, 0, …, 0) for every n.” The dependency bodies support the intended meanings: `allEntriesZero T` says every entry coerces to `0`; `rowPartitionFun` has parts `if ↑i = 0 then n else 0`; and `IsYamanouchi` requires semistandardness and, for every `j > 0`, that `nu + contentColGeq T j` is weakly decreasing. The binder `(hN : 0 < N)` is carried by the informal row-partition definition, which explicitly “Requires N > 0,” so it is not an added contentful restriction. The formal theorem is actually more general in allowing arbitrary `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ`, rather than requiring them to be N-partitions with `mu ⊆ lam`; this weaker shape context does not prevent it from implying the blueprint statement for valid skew shapes.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.alte.justification: The blueprint fixes only “an $N\in\mathbb N$” and states $a_\rho=\prod_{1\le i<j\le N}(x_i-x_j)$, with no assumption that $N\ne0$. The elaborated signature adds the binder `∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]`, restricting the identity to positive `N`. This is mathematically contentful rather than merely an encoding requirement: the definitions `rhoVector N : Fin N → ℕ`, `alternant N ...`, and the finite products are all meaningful for `N = 0`, where both sides are empty constructions and the identity should still be stated. Apart from this restriction, `rhoVector` gives `(N-1,…,0)`, the alternant body matches the determinant convention, and `∏ i, ∏ j with j > i, (X i - X j)` is the zero-based form of the product over `i<j`. Remove `[NeZero N]` from `alternant_rho_eq_vandermonde` (and from any proof dependency that forces it) to make the declaration faithful.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.esym.justification: The target states exactly that for `n : ℕ` with `hn : n ≤ N`, `MvPolynomial.esymm (Fin N) R n = SymmetricFunctions.schur (SymmetricFunctions.NPartition.colPartition N n hn)`, matching “For $n \leq N$, the elementary symmetric polynomial $e_n$ equals the Schur polynomial indexed by the column partition.” The dependency `colPartition` has parts `if ↑i < n then 1 else 0`, hence represents $(1^n,0^{N-n})`; `MvPolynomial.esymm` is documented as the sum of degree-`n` squarefree monomials; and `schur` is defined as the sum of `T.toMonomial` over all SSYT, matching the informal definitions. The use of variables indexed by `Fin N` is explicitly sanctioned by the informal convention. The binder `[CommRing R]` supplies the coefficient setting required by the project’s `schur` definition, and quantifying over every commutative ring is at least as general as the unspecified coefficient setting of the blueprint, not a weakening.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.ftsf.justification: Parts of the package are faithful, but the h- and p-statements add mathematically substantive domain assumptions absent from the blueprint. For (b), the blueprint fixes only “Fix a commutative ring K,” whereas `hsymm_algebraicIndependent` and `hsymm_generates_symmetric` quantify with `[CommRing K] ... [IsDomain K]`. Thus they establish algebraic independence and unique generation only for integral domains, not for every commutative ring. The extra `[DecidableEq (Fin N)]` is merely an encoding requirement for `MvPolynomial.hsymm`, not substantive drift. For (c), the blueprint says “assume that K is a commutative ℚ-algebra,” while `psum_algebraicIndependent` and `psum_generates_symmetric` require both `[Algebra ℚ K] [IsDomain K]`; a commutative ℚ-algebra need not be a domain, so `[IsDomain K]` again narrows the theorem. Remove `[IsDomain K]` from those four declarations (and adjust their proofs/dependencies) to match the stated scope. By contrast, `esymm_algebraicIndependent`, `esymm_generates_symmetric`, and `esymmAlgEquiv'` use only `[CommRing K]` and correctly express part (a); the families indexed by `i : Fin N` with degree `↑i + 1` are exactly e₁,…,e_N, h₁,…,h_N, and p₁,…,p_N.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.hsym.justification: The target quantifies `∀ {N : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (hN : 0 < N) (n : ℕ)` and asserts `MvPolynomial.hsymm (Fin N) R n = SymmetricFunctions.schur (SymmetricFunctions.NPartition.rowPartition N n hN)`, exactly matching “For $N>0$, ... $h_n=s_{(n,0,\ldots,0)}$.” The dependency `rowPartition` has parts `if ↑i = 0 then n else 0`, so it is precisely the stated row partition, while `schur` is the sum over all SSYTs and `SSYT.toMonomial` is the product of variables over tableau boxes, matching the informal definitions of $s_\lambda$ and $x_T$. The base-library `MvPolynomial.hsymm` is documented as the sum of all degree-$n$ monomials, matching the informal complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial. Using `Fin N` indexes the same $N$ variables with zero-based rather than one-based labels. Quantifying over all commutative rings rather than retaining a fixed chapter-level ring is harmless generality.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.jt-e.justification: The target conflates the two independent bounds. The blueprint quantifies an ambient partition size and separately says, “Let M ∈ ℕ be such that both λᵗ and μᵗ have length ≤ M,” with an M×M determinant. But the elaborated signature has only `{N : ℕ}` and binds all four tuples as `(lam mu lamt muT : Fin N → ℕ)`, while the determinant is indexed by `Fin N`. Consequently it only proves the case M = N and additionally requires λ and μ themselves to fit into N-tuples. For example, a partition may have more than M rows while its transpose has length ≤ M; such a case is covered by the blueprint but cannot be supplied to this target. This restriction enters at the target binders, not at `NPartition.IsTranspose`, whose signature already supports separate lengths `{N M : ℕ}`. A faithful signature should have separate `{N M : ℕ}`, take `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ` and `lamt muT : Fin M → ℕ`, use `IsTranspose lam lamt` and `IsTranspose mu muT`, and take the determinant over `Fin M` (while the elementary polynomials remain in the ambient polynomial variables, here `Fin N`). Moreover, the target adds `(hcontained : ∀ i, mu i ≤ lam i)`, whereas the informal statement merely says “Let λ and μ be two partitions” and its supplied skew-Schur definition likewise does not state containment. This is a further mathematically substantive added hypothesis, introduced because `SkewPartition.mk` requires `inner ≤ outer`; to match the literal blueprint, the skew-Schur dependency would need to support arbitrary pairs, or the blueprint would need to assume μ ⊆ λ.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.jt-h.justification: The blueprint quantifies over “two M-partitions” and imposes no containment hypothesis before asserting the identity. The target instead has the additional binder `hcontained : ∀ (i : Fin N), mu i ≤ lam i`. Moreover, this restriction is forced by the dependency `SymmetricFunctions.SkewPartition.mk`, whose third argument is `inner ≤ outer`, together with `NPartition.partLE`, whose body is `∀ i, mu.parts i ≤ lam.parts i`; `SymmetricFunctions.skewSchur` only accepts such a `SkewPartition`. Thus the blueprint’s claimed `s_{λ/μ}` for arbitrary pairs of partitions cannot be stated using the supplied project definition, rather than merely being omitted by the target. To make it statable and faithful, `SkewPartition`/`skewSchur` and their tableau dependencies would need to be generalized to arbitrary pairs of partitions with a specified meaning for noncontained pairs. Alternatively, the informal theorem would need an explicit assumption `μ ⊆ λ`, in which case the present target would match it.

The target exactly states the non-skew Jacobi–Trudi identity. Its binders `(lam : Fin N → ℕ) (hlam : ∀ (i j : Fin N), i ≤ j → lam j ≤ lam i)` encode that λ is a weakly decreasing nonnegative partition, via `NPartition.mk`. The right side uses `jacobiTrudiMatrixH lam (fun x => 0)`, matching the blueprint’s “μ = 0”; by its body, entry `(i,j)` is `hsymmExt (↑(lam i) - 0 - ↑i + ↑j)`, hence `h_{λᵢ-i+j}`. Using zero-based `Fin N` indices does not alter `-i+j` from the blueprint’s one-based indexing. The dependency `hsymmExt` also matches the supplied convention `h_n = 0` for `n < 0` and `h_0 = 1`. Finally, `schur` is the tableau-sum Schur polynomial of the partition. The universal coefficient binder `[CommRing R]` makes the theorem valid over every commutative ring and therefore is more general than, rather than a restriction of, the unspecified coefficient setting in the blueprint.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.jt-m.justification: The blueprint asserts: “The determinant of the Jacobi–Trudi matrix det(H) is a symmetric polynomial.” The target concludes exactly `(SymmetricFunctions.jacobiTrudiMatrixH lam mu).det.IsSymmetric`. stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.jt-o.justification: The target states exactly the claimed identity: “∀ {N : ℕ} … (a c : ℤ), ∑ p ∈ …latticePathFinset a c, p.weight = …hsymmExt (c - a),” matching “Let a and c be two integers” and the sum of path weights from “(a,1) to (c,N)” equaling “h_{c-a}.” The dependency bodies implement the intended notions: `latticePathFinset` is all encoded paths when `c ≥ a` and empty when `c < a`; `LatticePath` records the weakly increasing sequence of east-step heights; `weight` multiplies the corresponding variables `MvPolynomial.X j`, matching east-step weight `x_{y-1}` under the `Fin N` indexing; and `hsymmExt` gives `0` for negative indices and `MvPolynomial.hsymm … n.toNat` otherwise, including `h₀ = 1`. stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.lgv-.justification: The elaborated target adds the hypothesis `0 < N` in `∀ {N : ℕ} ... stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.lr-z.justification: The target quantifies over all three N-partitions—`(lam mu nu : Fin N → ℕ)` with separate `IsNPartition` hypotheses—but does not assume `mu ⊆ lam`. stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.omeg.justification: The blueprint states, “The ω-involution is bijective.” The target asserts exactly `Function.Bijective ⇑(SymmetricFunctions.omegaInvolution hn)`. stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.skew.justification: The target restricts the theorem to `∀ {N : ℕ} [inst : NeZero N]`, whereas the blueprint fixes merely “an `N ∈ ℕ`” and says “any two `N`-partitions”; its definition of `[n]` explicitly covers `n = 0`. stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sign.q-.justification: The formal binders exactly match the blueprint assumptions: `∀ {K : Type u_1} [Field K] (d : ℕ), 0 < d → ∀ (ω : K), IsPrimitiveRoot ω d → ∀ (n k : ℕ)`.
